name: "Kiwi" — the New Zealand medic
role: Medic on the mountain; a New Zealander, Larry says
summary: The medic Larry held sick call with on Núi Bà Đen, for the Cambodians and their families: "Captain Kennedy handled the political problems. Me and the medic handled the sick call. I called the medic Kiwi, he was a new Zealander. We went to Saigon together probably 15 times. We met Tototz down there all the time. I don't remember the medics name at all. Might have been Roger."
researchNotes: New on 2026-09-05 (data/recollections/giscus-vn-0041-c18308745.json). New Zealand's military presence in Vietnam in 1964–65 was small (a small engineer team from June 1964, an artillery battery from July 1965), so a New Zealander serving as a medic at a U.S. Special Forces camp in Tây Ninh would be an exception someone recorded. Two readings to keep apart: a New Zealand serviceman attached to the camp, or a New Zealand-born man in the U.S. Army. The first is a search in New Zealand records (Archives New Zealand, the NZ Vietnam veterans' rolls); the second is a morning-report question like the other names here. Neither search has been run. He has said he does not remember the name, and 'Roger' is the most he has. 2026-09-15, on his son's decision (no spelling notes on public pages): the rendered aliases were trimmed; removed from display, kept here: "Roger (Larry: "might have been Roger")".
